# readme-writer

> An Agent Skill (Python, MIT, v0.2.0) that writes and repairs human-facing READMEs, the page a visitor opens first and the one surface an LLM grounds on from a pasted repo URL. Its starting condition: the reader must be able to say what the repository is for before any mechanism or install step. Code extracts evidence (`readme_evidence.py`, JSON, no verdict), a fresh-context judge agent (`readme-judge`) returns a named verdict (Publishable / Fix / Rewrite), a two-round revision cap and a review panel follow, and the author's read-through is the final gate. Human-surface counterpart to llms-txt-writer.

## Core documentation

- [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt): self-contained Q&A reference for AI agents (facts, the purpose-first condition, evidence vs verdict, the loop, what the skill enforces)
- [README.md](README.md): human-facing narrative (why it exists, how it works, what it enforces, install, when to use)
- [SKILL.md](skills/readme-writer/SKILL.md): full skill specification: the information floor, visual rules, length budget, voice and register, the 11-step workflow, anti-patterns
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): release notes (v0.2.0 evidence + judge redesign; v0.1.0 initial lint-based release)

## Architecture

- [scripts/readme_evidence.py](skills/readme-writer/scripts/readme_evidence.py): deterministic evidence extractor (stdlib only). Emits JSON (or `--text`): first-screen length and new terms, identity lead, ADR / sibling-repo / docs references, coined-term candidates, `<details>` contents, figures with prose-after check, badges, slop words and em-dashes, internal-history lines, numeric claims, DOI / citation presence. No score, no threshold; exit 0 always, 2 only on missing or oversized file
- [references/readme-judge-checklist.md](skills/readme-writer/references/readme-judge-checklist.md): the judge's fixed checklist: first screen (R1-R3), sentence density (R4-R9), context budget (R10-R14), and six questions generalized from author findings (K1-K6: as-of consistency, accretion detection, claim logic, unresolved references, missing purpose, promises without destinations)
- [references/visual.md](skills/readme-writer/references/visual.md), [references/ja-register.md](skills/readme-writer/references/ja-register.md), [references/about.md](skills/readme-writer/references/about.md): diagram rules, Japanese register table, GitHub About description / topics procedure
- [tests/test_readme_evidence.py](skills/readme-writer/tests/test_readme_evidence.py): unit + integration tests over the extractor
- [fixtures/](skills/readme-writer/fixtures/) and [evals/fixtures/](skills/readme-writer/evals/fixtures/): clean and issue-laden sample READMEs, plus pre-rewrite real READMEs with expected judge findings for smoke-testing the judge
- [inspiration.md](skills/readme-writer/inspiration.md): design sources and calibration notes, kept out of SKILL.md for portability
- Judge and reviewer agents (`readme-judge`, `readme-reviewer`, `readme-clarity-reviewer`) are published in [claude-harness](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-harness) under `agents/`

## Grounding

- AKC ADR-0008 "Code-LLM Layering": code counts, LLM judges: [agent-knowledge-cycle](https://github.com/shimo4228/agent-knowledge-cycle), concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19200726
- Authorship Strategy ADR-0006 (LLM-first ingest, dual entry points): this skill covers the third, human-facing surface: [authorship-strategy](https://github.com/shimo4228/authorship-strategy), concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20263316
- llm-as-judge skill: the judge's form (binary checks with quoted evidence, refutation pass, non-aggregated named verdict): [llm-as-judge](https://github.com/shimo4228/llm-as-judge)

## Sibling skills

- [llms-txt-writer](https://github.com/shimo4228/llms-txt-writer): the AI-surface counterpart (`llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt`)
- [jsonld-knowledge-graph](https://github.com/shimo4228/jsonld-knowledge-graph): companion JSON-LD graph for the concept surface
- [context-sync](https://github.com/shimo4228/context-sync): audits cross-surface fact consistency (README vs machine layer)
- [claude-skill-writing-ecosystem](https://github.com/shimo4228/claude-skill-writing-ecosystem): orchestrator for long-form human prose (articles, essays)
